rows.question: Which price source may be retained, at what latency, and with what right to republish a derived line?
rows.known: The NFL's own betting FAQ states its odds are a partner widget; the repository holds one community observation with no bookmaker identity.
rows.unknown: No licensed archive, no terms of reuse, no open-versus-close flag on the stored numbers.
rows.discovery: Obtain a written data agreement covering history, latency, retention and derived output, or explicitly accept a community source and label every price as such forever.

rows.question: If the only source is community, is a community price good enough to define an opening line?
rows.known: The stored series is digest-verified and has one observation. 411 of 816 market cells are post-hoc or empty.
rows.unknown: Whether the release's price is an open, a close or a snapshot of one book.
rows.discovery: Capture the same markets from a second, independent source and compare: if the two disagree by more than a point, neither can define an opening.

rows.question: How do we know a listed player actually missed the game?
rows.known: 6 of 254 report rows carry a game designation; no inactive list is held.
rows.unknown: Which listed players were inactive, and which played a reduced role.
rows.discovery: Capture official inactive lists for each game and join them to the report rows; the play rate per designation is then measurable.

rows.question: Is 'no injury section' the same as 'no injuries'?
rows.known: 4 clubs had no section on the captured report, and 24 of 32 clubs had rows at all.
rows.unknown: Whether an absent section reflects a healthy roster or a reporting gap.
rows.discovery: Compare a club's absent-section week with its next published report and with its inactive list; a reappearing long-term injury would prove a gap.

rows.question: What does a published rank actually mean when one slot names three players?
rows.known: 149 rank-1 slots name two or more players.
rows.unknown: Which of those players starts, and whether the order within the group is meaningful.
rows.discovery: Join playing time to each shared slot: if the measured shares are indistinguishable, the slot is a committee and no single starter exists.
rows.source_label: NFL injury report (OFFICIAL); club charts: decision-lab/data/official_snapshot.json

rows.question: Can depth be derived from playing time for a player who has not yet played?
rows.known: Snap counts cover the season to date; a rookie with no snaps has no measurement.
rows.unknown: The order behind a player with zero recorded snaps.
rows.discovery: Keep the published order for those players and label the measured order as unavailable for them; do not fall back to jersey number.

rows.question: Two clubs publish no parseable depth chart. What is the authorised structured source?
rows.known: The Texans publish the chart as an image and the Packers prepend jersey numbers; the failure is recorded per club.
rows.unknown: A structured, authorised source for those two clubs.
rows.discovery: Ask each club for a structured export, or accept the gap and publish it as a gap rather than transcribing an image by eye.

rows.question: Is the injury effect even measurable at this sample size?
rows.known: The holdout ablation interval spans zero for every λ in the published grid.
rows.unknown: The size of the true effect, and whether it is larger for specific positions.
rows.discovery: Accumulate pre-kickoff price and availability captures across a season, then re-run the ablation with position-specific terms and a pre-registered λ.

rows.question: Which estimator should represent the side?
rows.known: Two estimators exist: a ridge fit on seasonal scoring and a leak-free Elo. Both trail the market on the same 137 games, and their errors correlate at about 0.95.
rows.unknown: Whether a third family, or a combination, would close the gap.
rows.discovery: Publish both until a walk-forward comparison separates them with an interval, which requires more pre-kickoff games.

rows.question: What converts a measured snap share into points of margin?
rows.known: The ablation publishes a pre-registered λ grid so no single conversion is asserted.
rows.unknown: The true conversion, and whether it varies by position.
rows.discovery: Fit λ out of sample on a corpus large enough to estimate it, and pre-register the fit before looking at the holdout.

rows.question: What sample is enough to call a strategy validated?
rows.known: Floors are pre-registered at n≥50 to publish and n≥200 to promote; the largest scored arm has 137.
rows.unknown: Whether those floors are strict enough given the dependence between legs in the same week.
rows.discovery: Simulate the family-wise error rate under the current floors and adjust them before the next evaluation window opens.

rows.question: Where do the rewards come from, and who funds them?
rows.known: No reward pool, rule set or funding source exists in the repository.
rows.unknown: The existence, size and legality of any reward.
rows.discovery: Decide the jurisdiction and the funding source before any reward is described as available.

rows.question: Are control arms scored on the same rows as the model arms?
rows.known: Yes by construction, and a control's Brier skill is exactly zero, which is what proves the scoring path is neutral.
rows.unknown: Whether a control should also carry an interval on its own win rate for display.
rows.discovery: Add a Wilson interval to every control arm so a reader can see that a 51% control is ordinary.

rows.question: What would a validated joint probability require?
rows.known: Nothing exists yet: no prop outcome feed and no operator settlement rules.
rows.unknown: The conditional structure between legs inside a game.
rows.discovery: Capture a play-level prop outcome series and a same-game price pair; only then can a joint model be fitted and validated on a holdout.

rows.question: What may be republished from each source, and under what terms?
rows.known: The site links to official pages and stores a private capture; reuse terms are not established.
rows.unknown: Whether derived output (a fair line) counts as republished source data.
rows.discovery: Get written terms per source class, or restrict the site to derived analysis plus links.

rows.question: What runs the capture schedule, and what happens when a capture is missed?
rows.known: Captures are scripted and hashed; no schedule currently hits the official page on Wed/Thu/Fri.
rows.unknown: Whether a missed capture can be detected and recorded as a gap rather than back-filled.
rows.discovery: Enable a scheduled capture job, write a manifest of expected captures, and fail the build when a scheduled capture is absent.

rows.question: How should a source change be distinguished from a data error?
rows.known: The build fails closed on a reconciliation break and publishes drift instead of reconciling it.
rows.unknown: The threshold at which a row-count change is a source format change rather than news.
rows.discovery: Pin an expected row count and field set per source, and alert on a miss before the page is published.

rows.question: Which operator's void and push rules govern a graded bet?
rows.known: Grading uses a mechanical push rule stated in policy P06; no operator terms are held.
rows.unknown: Whether a real operator voids a pushed leg or refunds the stake inside a same-game parlay.
rows.discovery: Obtain the rules for whichever operator would be used, and store them with a date.

rows.question: Which of the 62 requirements should be funded first?
rows.known: The suggestions page ranks 9 proposals by the requirements they unblock.
rows.unknown: The owner's appetite for a licensed price feed, which would unblock the most at once.
rows.discovery: Choose a path on the suggestions page, then re-run the build: blocked gates become a plan rather than a list.

rows.question: How does a demoted strategy earn its way back?
rows.known: Demotion is automatic and published, and the score is retained.
rows.unknown: The re-entry rule, and whether a demoted rule must be re-registered with a new hash.
rows.discovery: Require re-registration (a new hash) with the demotion recorded in its text, so a comeback cannot silently reuse a failed rule.
